name: Serenity Palace
reason: Source 'Beiyou Palace' (the destroyed force in the Arctic, origin of the Heavenly Feather Saint Crown, ch 479) was renamed 'Serenity Palace' to fit the Western fantasy register of the adaptation.
description: A destroyed palace in the Arctic Lands and the former seat of the Holy Maiden, said to have possessed many Relic-Class weapons before her defeat. It is the origin of the Heavenly Feather Crown presented in Ep 492.

name: Time Copper Coin
reason: Source saint artifact 'Copper Coin of Time' (chs 479-481) was lightly reordered to 'Time Copper Coin' for the adaptation, with its Saint-grade tier rendered as Relic-Class.
description: The World Merchants' Guild's one publicly known Relic-Class weapon. It contains a sliver of the Time Law and grants its bearer six extra hours of cultivation daily; in the source it sustained the guild's ancient giant's long lifespan.

name: Soul-Nurturing Elixir
reason: Source item 'Soul Nourishing Pill' (ch 491) was localized as 'Soul-Nurturing Elixir', converting the Chinese 'pill' convention into the Western 'elixir' register.
description: A restorative consumed to replenish soul power strained while drawing runes. Ep 504 mocks lesser Rune Masters who bathe, burn incense, and down a Soul-Nurturing Elixir after a single half-finished rune.

name: Soul-Nurturing Heartstone
reason: No source counterpart was identified; the name appears to be an adaptation-coined soul-restorative treasure in the same register as the Soul-Nurturing Elixir.
description: A precious soul-nourishing stone given as an apology in Ep 505, during the Rune Tower arc. Distinct from the consumable Soul-Nurturing Elixir.

name: Cloud Leopard
reason: Source God Beast 'Cloud-Piercing Leopard' (ch 494) was shortened to 'Cloud Leopard' for the adaptation.
description: A God Beast bloodline. In Ep 507 onlookers deduce that a fighter's transformation proves he carries an extremely high concentration of Cloud Leopard blood (the source's Ao Xiang and his Cloud-Piercing Leopard bloodline).

name: Corpse Parasite
reason: The source's 'Three Corpses Gu' (ch 494), a vicious gu insect technique, was localized as 'Corpse Parasite' to drop the culture-specific 'gu' concept.
description: A vile parasitic insect: its host gains an unstoppable surge of power but becomes a walking corpse whose mind and soul are devoured, denied even reincarnation. Owen nearly used one on himself in Ep 507 before Marilyn exposed it.

name: Pristine Essence
reason: The source concept 'Primordial Yin' (ch 733), a maiden's virgin yin essence, was euphemized as 'Pristine Essence' to remove the yin/yang cultivation jargon.
description: A maiden's innate pure essence prized for rituals. Maddox dismisses Cora as worthless for ritual purposes once her Pristine Essence is gone, Zane having taken it (Eps 753-756).

name: Joel
reason: A US-origin first name assigned to a minor tournament fighter; no named source counterpart appears in the evidence for the corresponding chapters.
description: A fighter from Mysterious Luna Hall in the Martial Tournament. Though more advanced than Brent, he was defeated and sent crashing down by Brent's devastating strikes in Ep 509.

name: Davis Brandt
reason: A full US-style name given to a minor tournament opponent; the source scene (chs 495-496) features Luo Zheng refusing matches with exemption cards but presents no named counterpart for this fighter.
description: A fighter of the Black Mountain Order at the primary level of the Core-Forged Realm, drawn against Zane in the Martial Tournament. Zane refused the match with an exemption card, baffling the crowd since Davis was considered weaker than Eden or Brent (Ep 509).

name: Ian
reason: A US-origin first name assigned to a minor Ethereal Spirit Sect disciple; no named source counterpart appears in the evidence.
description: A Celestial-level talent of the Ethereal Spirit Sect and its former pride until Brent displaced him. Watching the Martial Tournament, Brent's admission that Zane might be the better cultivator shook Ian's confidence to its core (Eps 510-511).

name: Angel of Death
reason: The source creature 'Cilie' (ch 499), whose baby's eye was sealed in a crystal from the Arctic Ice Plains, was renamed 'Angel of Death' for an evocative Western register.
description: A legendary creature and the natural mortal enemy of the True Dragon. The third eye of a young Angel of Death, retrieved from the Arctic Icecap four thousand years ago by Cloud Hall's thirteenth leader and refined for three uses, serves as a sect-saving trump card capable of killing False Tribulation Realm experts; Tia wields it in Eps 512-513.

name: Lantern Festival
reason: The source's 'Lantern Festival' / 'Lantern Lighting Festival' (chs 512, 516) was carried over directly.
description: The gathering at which all warriors possessing an Enchanted Lamp (the source's Spirit Lamp of the Immortal Tomb) are summoned to light them, announced five days in advance by the World Merchants' Guild as the key to entering the Immortal's Tomb (Eps 526, 530).

name: South Sea
reason: The source location 'South Sea' (ch 513) was carried over unchanged.
description: A sea region south of the Heartlands. Maddox spent three months on a journey there with his son (Ep 527); in the source, Cui Xie prepared for the Immortal Tomb on a South Sea island.

name: White Emperor City
reason: The source location 'White Emperor City' (chs 93-634), the human stronghold on the Asura Battlefield, was carried over unchanged.
description: A human stronghold on the Asura Battlefield where Zane once trained and faced demonic energy from Demon Soldiers, Demon Generals, and even a Demon King. Survivors of the demon invasion fled east and tore open a space crack for their staging ground (Ep 534).

name: Demon Emperor
reason: The Ep 535 usage corresponds to the source's 'Yin Corpse Demon Emperor' (chs 520-521), a Demon Emperor-grade Yin Corpse; the adaptation shortened it to 'Demon Emperor'.
description: A Demon Emperor-level undead Yin Corpse fought in the Immortal Tomb arc; Zane's merged projectile blasted toward it as it revealed itself (Ep 535). 'Demon Emperor' also functions as the rank above Demon King in the demon hierarchy.

name: Dreamy Swampland
reason: Source location 'Cloud Dream Swamp' (chs 523, 528) was renamed 'Dreamy Swampland' for the Western fantasy register.
description: A desolate swamp into which the Poison King Simon was driven after every major faction hunted him eight thousand miles across the Heartlands; he lived there like an animal for decades (Ep 537).

name: Starlight Astrology
reason: The source divination art 'Purple Star Astrology' (ch 540, mastered by Immortal Heavenly Mist) was renamed 'Starlight Astrology' for the adaptation.
description: A fate-reading divination art. Its master's star-reading revealed to him what Zane could not yet see: that Elara wasn't just a captive (Ep 554).

name: Lori
issues: Episode gender_signal reads m2/f0, but the episode text ('She knelt to feed him', 'she gasped') and the source counterpart Ah Lian are unambiguously female; the pronoun count is extraction noise.
reason: The village girl 'Ah Lian' (ch 542) was given the US-origin name 'Lori', matching the scene-for-scene adaptation of Luo Zheng's arrival on the new continent.
description: A young village girl who, with a boy her age, finds the paralyzed Zane after his crash-landing in the new world; she later brings him flatbread and water, and is nearly seized by an ogre slaver (Eps 556-557).

name: Greater Legendary Beast the Celestial Chimera
issues: Dossier name is a tier-plus-name compound from the apposition 'Greater Legendary Beast, the Celestial Chimera'; the entity proper is the Celestial Chimera, with 'Greater Legendary Beast' being its tier.
reason: The source super God Beast 'Qilin' (ch 547, close relative of the Cloud Chasing Lion) was renamed 'Celestial Chimera' to replace the Chinese mythological creature with a Western-legible one.
description: A Greater Legendary Beast (the source's super God Beast / Mythological Beast tier) and close relative of the Cloud-Chaser Lion, whose bone Zane claimed from Vesper's Celestial Tomb to temper his body (Eps 561-562).

name: Tower of Sin I
issues: The surface string 'Tower of Sin I' never occurs in the episode text; it is an extraction artifact (sentence-boundary pronoun 'I' glued onto 'Tower of Sin'). Mentions belong to the Tower of Sin.

name: War Sages and Soul Sea Realm
reason: Extraction fragment from 'it killed War Sages and Soul Sea Realm masters' (Ep 634); not an entity. Covered by the separate War Sage and Soul Sea Realm entries.

name: War Sages the Ogres
reason: Extraction fragment from 'the two War Sages the Ogres had been hiding in the Tower' (Ep 620); not an entity. Covered by War Sage and Ogres.

name: Tuesday
reason: A weekday name, not a story entity.

name: World's Battle
original_name: fate of battle of the worlds
issues: Extracted as the fragment 'World's Battle'; the episodes' full term is 'Fate of the World's Battle' (Ep 616).
reason: The source destiny concept 'Fate of Battle of the Worlds' / 'fate of the Battle of the Great Era' (chs 540, 597) was smoothed into 'Fate of the World's Battle'.
description: The world-shaping destiny Zane carries. Lavender invokes it against the statue of the Demon Night's former Queen of Slaughter: no lump of stone can kill someone who bears the Fate of the World's Battle (Ep 616).

name: Demon Night War Sages
reason: Generic compound: War Sages belonging to the Demon Night clan (Eps 618, 944). Covered by the separate Demon Night and War Sage entries.

name: Heavenly Feather Sanctuary Zane
reason: Extraction artifact gluing the location 'Heavenly Feather Sanctuary' onto the adjacent name 'Zane'; not an entity. Covered by the separate Heavenly Feather Sanctuary and Zane Lowell entries.

name: Cursed Domain
reason: The source's 'Curse Domain' (ch 617), set up by the Curse Sector Lord, was localized as 'Cursed Domain'.
description: The domain power underlying the Cursed Land: in Ep 636 it is deduced that the Cursed Land is almost certainly the Cursed Domain of an ancient Sector Lord, mysteriously ineffective against anyone below a War Sage.

name: Bull-Toad
reason: The source's 'Giant Mangku Toad' (ch 620; also rendered 'Giant Python Toad' in chs 621-628) was renamed 'Bull-Toad' for a punchier Western creature name.
description: A legendary ferocious toad ruling the forbidden western area of the cave region, sitting at the top of the local food chain; its croak echoes for miles and it sweeps intruders away with its thick tongue (Eps 639-642).

name: Frost Wolf
reason: The source monster 'Azure Wolf' (chs 626-627, 630) was renamed 'Frost Wolf', consistent with the show's policy of avoiding 'Azure' (reserved away from the source Azure Dragon, localized as Cobalt Dragon).
description: A powerful wolf monster whose lair flanks one side of the Bloody Pass in the Dark Nether Cave, opposite the Shadow-maw's; travelers must pass in total silence to avoid waking the packs (Eps 645, 649).

name: Purgatory Fire Snakes
reason: The source creature name 'Purgatory Fire Snakes' (ch 628) was carried over unchanged.
description: A pair of dangerous fire snakes coiled in the deep cave region; a lesser threat than the monster swarm behind, but still a serious obstacle for Esther and Fabian's group (Eps 646-647).

name: Scorchplate
reason: The source tool 'Flaming Balance' (ch 630), which sprays pale blue flames when fed energy, was renamed 'Scorchplate' for the adaptation.
description: A mid-tier enchanted weapon that spews pale blue flames feared by the cave's demonic beasts. Timothy used it to break the monster siege and carve a path to the Bloody Pass (Eps 648-649).

name: Venomous Ghost Martens
reason: The source creature 'Poisonous Ghost Marten' (ch 632) was lightly reworded to 'Venomous Ghost Marten'.
description: Fearsome marten beasts, more than ten of which guard the remains of an ancient expert in the Mysterious Underworld Cave; too strong even for peak War Sages, they foiled the Demon Night clan's earlier attempts to reach the site (Ep 651).

name: Adolph
reason: The source's ancient expert 'Qing Yuanzi' (ch 632), whose remains and treasure the party seeks, was given the Western name 'Adolph'.
description: A long-dead powerful expert whose remains and legacy lie guarded in the deep cave region. Esther asks the Queen who Adolph is when his name comes up in connection with the marked treasure site (Ep 651).

name: Dark Sky Mage
reason: A renamed legendary source figure from the Xuanming ('dark nether') lore that also yields the Dark Nether Cave and Death Light; no direct source name for the mage himself appears in the evidence.
description: A legendary freelance powerhouse from the Heartlands who wielded the power of a world lord but never claimed a world, feared by all who knew his name. The Ogres hold the Fruit of the Dark Sky Mage, which can unlock a devastating secret technique if paired with his complete inheritance (Ep 655).

name: Sanctum of Eternal Night
reason: Localized name for the Twilight Group's holy land, following the source's clan holy-land structure (the Nether Night clan's Holy Land); no exact source term appears in the evidence.
description: The holy land of the Twilight Group on the Sea God Continent, protected by the Ogre sacred lands, which explains the Twilight Group's unwavering loyalty to the Ogres (Eps 666, 675).

name: Murderous Rats
reason: The source's 'fierce rats' (ch 650) were renamed 'Murderous Rats' for a more menacing register.
description: Deceptively docile-looking rat beasts that swarm in overwhelming numbers, agile enough to slip into armor and strip flesh; they beset Zane's party after the fall into the depths (Eps 669-670, the Ep 669 title creature).

name: Shadow Pearl
reason: The source treasure 'Black Spirit Pearl' (ch 663), harvested from Black and Blue Mussels, was renamed 'Shadow Pearl'.
description: A priceless pill-crafting ingredient with a chance of being found in the body of a slain sea creature; a major source of income for the local sect, which demands daily quotas of the pearls from its divers (Ep 683).

name: Holt
reason: Source 'Sect Elder Hu' of the Fish Dragon Sect (ch 664) was localized as 'Elder Holt', keeping the H- initial while westernizing the surname.
description: An elder of the Sea Wyrm Sect (the source's Fish Dragon Sect) who ordered his men to kill the injured Zane regardless of his condition, dismissing his would-be victims' resistance as a death wish; his ambush ended badly for him (Eps 684-687).
